title: An SVG logo comes into a video and stays sharp at any size
goal: Today an SVG dropped or imported into a video is refused with a note asking for a PNG. The title walkthrough mock puts SVG art (Sparkle, Star, Cursor, Dot) on the Library shelf and promises it stays crisp blown up on a 4K frame, so an SVG should come in like a PNG and be drawn sharp at whatever size it is shown or exported.
notes: Follow-up from a-logo-or-picture-can-be-brought-into-a-video-fo, which shipped the refusal (MediaFiles.vectorRefusal, CanvasFileDrop.vector, LibraryImport.notYet). Finding: macOS reads SVG already: NSImage(contentsOf:) on an .svg returns an _NSSVGImageRep that draws as a vector at any size; CGImageSource cannot (count 0). The gap is the model: pixels live in ImageStore as one CGImage per ImageRef, so sharp-at-any-size needs ImageStore to keep the SVG data and rasterize per render scale (DocumentRenderer asks at the composite scale), plus PackageIO writing the .svg bytes. Fixture: Scripts/playtest/fixtures/logo/Acme Logo.svg. Mock: docs/design/mocks/pages/video-title-wt.html steps 6-8.
acceptance: Import Media, a Finder drop on the Library shelf, the canvas and the timeline all take an SVG; the refusal note is gone
An SVG logo scaled to fill a 4K export is as sharp as the same art drawn at its own size (measured edge sharpness within a set margin of a native render)
The SVG travels inside a saved project and opens again sharp
A walk at Next defaults covers the SVG path and passes
An art tile on the Media shelf captions like the mock: its name over its kind (Sparkle / svg), or a decision card says why not

log.note: also: the mock's art tiles caption as the name over its kind (Sparkle / svg); a picture tile today says the file name with its extension over its pixel size (Acme Logo.png / 480 x 192), the way recording tiles already say Tutorial Sample.mp4 / 0:08. Settle the art tile's two lines with the SVG tiles.

before building: a Premiere/Photoshop user expects an SVG to behave like any picture and stay crisp (Photoshop places SVG as a smart object). Gaps found: the store keeps one bitmap per picture, the render module may not import AppKit (macOS only draws SVG through NSImage), .svgz is not readable by macOS, and a picture FILE from the Finder on the timeline had no ghost and landed mid-canvas (PNG too). Decided: keep the SVG bytes beside a stand-in bitmap, have the app hand the renderer an NSImage reader at launch, draw at the frame's output pixels in quarter-octave steps, write images/<id>.svg in packages, drop svgz, and land Finder picture files on a Gfx track + the shelf like Premiere.

after building: walked library-svg-logo-walk at Next defaults (green, 6 real captures, screen unlocked). Opened every audit picture: shelf tile reads Acme Logo / svg with the whole logo centred (matched the mock's .th.art after fitting art instead of cropping), timeline tile lands on Gfx 0:02-0:07, Finder SVG lands on the canvas and on the timeline (ghost says Picture · New Gfx · 0:01), and the 2x render plus the 4x edge sheet show the SVG hard and the PNG soft. Measured bar in VectorArtTests: edge ramp 2px (native 0) vs 12px for the bitmap.

left rough (none clear the follow-up bar, kept here): .svgz not taken (macOS cannot draw it); an SVG on a collage slot lands as its own layer; opening an SVG with no document open still does nothing; the shelf thumbnail of an SVG is drawn from its own-size picture, so a tiny SVG can read slightly soft in the tile.

SVGs come into a video from Import Media, a Library drop, the canvas and the timeline, and are drawn at the frame's output pixels (VectorArt + ImageStore + DocumentRenderer), so a logo filling a 4K frame keeps hard edges (edge ramp 2px vs 12px for a bitmap, VectorArtTests). Packages carry images/<id>.svg and reopen sharp. Art tiles read name over kind (Acme Logo / svg). Finder picture files on the timeline land on a Gfx track. Verified: Scripts/test.sh 13393 green, library-svg-logo-walk at Next defaults green with 6 real captures, 13 related walks green. Audit queue/audits/2026-10-16-svg-logo.json. Commit cbea81b5.
